relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with confirmed SSADH deficiency and a homozygous variant: "We report an adolescent female with SSADHD".
method_note: Single-patient case report read in full; no tables. Output built with a short Python script from my own reading; every span checked verbatim against the paper by script. Scope: the patient plus her two parents, who were tested ('This allele was confirmed as heterozygous in both parents.'); parents labelled 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2' because the paper gives no per-parent sex. The patient is 'The second of two sibs'; the sibling is not described further (no testing, no affected status) and gets no row. The gene symbol ALDH5A1 is printed only in a reference title (Akaboshi 2003), not tied to this patient's variant, so gene_symbol_as_stated is 'not reported'. Variant printed as 'c.160-161delCT' (deletion of two nucleotides in exon 1); no transcript or protein given; variant type recorded as 'other' from 'deletion of two nucleotides' (paper does not say frameshift). Inheritance: both parents heterozygous carriers of the patient's homozygous allele (biparental); the enum has no value for both parents, so inheritance is left 'not reported' and the statement is quoted in parental_testing_statement. The variant is said to be 'as previously described by Akaboshi et al. 2003'; this refers to the allele, not to the patient, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null. Year: published online 22 August 2012, copyright line 2013; year recorded as 2013 from the copyright line. Age at diagnosis not stated (diagnosis appears to follow the age-14 episode, but no age is given), so left 'not reported'. 'possible limbic encephalitis' is hedged and not recorded as a feature. 'EEG abnormalities at 3 years of age': onset 3 years attached only to the EEG item, since the list sentence is ambiguous. Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormalities per D-27; the normal basic metabolic panel, cranial MRI at 1 year, hematological panels, hormonal assays and CSF parameters are whole investigations and are recorded as the paper names them, excluding nothing more specific. Checklist T2 hyperintensity of globus pallidus/subthalamic/dentate nuclei left 'not reported': MRI at 1 year was normal as a whole, and the age-14 MRI describes frontal, insular and temporal lesions only. Checklist cerebral atrophy marked observed from Fig. 4 'loss of parenchyma in the right temporal and insular areas' (focal, post-lesional). Psychiatric symptoms treated with olanzapine are unspecified, so the psychotic-symptoms checklist item is 'not reported'. 'Remained seizure-free' after MgVPA reintroduction is a treatment outcome, not an exclusion of seizures. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: Magnesium valproate (MgVPA) 20 mg/kg/day from 7 years, stopped at age 13; at age 14 intravenous acyclovir, ceftriaxone, dexamethasone and barbiturates plus enteral antiepileptics (carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, levetiracetam, phenobarbital), stopped due to adverse effects; olanzapine for psychiatric symptoms without benefit; MgVPA 15 mg/kg/day reintroduced at age 15 with seizure freedom and behavioral improvement one year later
span: MgVPA therapy (20 mg/kg/day) was introduced at 7 years based upon behavioral difficulties and EEG alterations, without observable adverse effects. At age 13, MgVPA was stopped

The patient was treated with acyclovir, ceftriaxone, dexamethasone and barbiturates intravenously, in addition to a number of enteral antiepileptics (carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, levetiracetam, phenobarbital). Intervention with antiepileptics was subsequently stopped due to adverse effects.
Olanzapine was prescribed for ensuing psychiatric symptoms, without evidence of clinical benefit.
At age 15 years, MgVPA (15 mg/kg/day) was reintroduced due to ongoing seizure activity and deteriorating behavior
One year following MgVPA reintroduction, our patient remained seizure-free with marked behavioral improvements.
